summary: Black Butte has held lookouts since 1910-11; a 1922 D-6 cupola still stands, the 1934 tower fell, and a 65-ft tower from 1995 was staffed in fire season as of 2019.

facts.design: 65-ft treated timber tower with 10x10-ft cab (1995), beside the 1922 D-6 cupola

access.note: Summit is a public hike on Deschutes National Forest land. The 65-ft tower is a staffed lookout; no source found says visitors may enter or climb it.

visit.trail_note: A road reaches most of the way up; the last two miles are on foot (2016 blog)

events.note: Firelookout.com dates the first tree crow's nest tower and tent to 1910; Forest Lookouts says the first lookout was established in 1911
Original D-6 cupola lookout; firelookout.com says about 1923 and a 2016 blog says 1923
Taller wooden tower built for better visibility; 82 or 83 ft; cab 7x7 or 8x8 ft depending on source
Log ground quarters cabin built; the NHLR says 1980, Forest Lookouts says 1979
1934 tower condemned after winter damage; the lookout duties went back to the cupola
Forest Service accepted a bid to build a 65-ft wood tower, lookout cab and communication building
Registered September 10, 1994 per the NHLR record
65-ft tower flown in sections by a Sikorsky Skycrane and assembled at the summit in May 1995
1934 tower collapsed under snow in December 2001 per Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com; the NHLR says the winter of 2002
Condemned ground quarters cabin burned by the Forest Service in November 2016
Volunteers restored the 1922 cupola; Friends of the Metolius raised the money; the article is dated September 2019

corrections.why: The 1994 contract, the 1995 erection and the 2019 Nugget article all describe a 65-ft tower; 3.0 m does not match any structure on the summit.

corrections.proposed: D-6 cupola (1922) is the original lookout; the staffed tower is a 65-ft timber tower (1995) with a 10x10 cab
corrections.why: D-6 is the cupola design, not the staffed tower; the brief's record attaches the cupola's design to the current tower.

corrections.proposed: 1934 tower built, condemned 1990, fell 2001 or 2002; current 65-ft tower built 1995
corrections.why: The 1934 tower no longer stands. The brief's 1934 build event describes a structure that has since been replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the first tree tower and tent to 1910; Forest Lookouts says a lookout was first established in 1911. The story gives both.
The NHLR and the 2019 Nugget say 1922; firelookout.com and a 2016 blog say about 1923. The story gives 1922 and notes the other date.

Newspaper quotes and a 1936 letter on Forest Lookouts say 83 ft with a 7x7 cage; the NHLR says 82 ft with a 7x7 cab; firelookout.com says 82 ft with an 8x8 cab. Announcements before the August 1934 opening said 85 and 87 ft. The story reports the disagreement.
Forest Lookouts and firelookout.com put the collapse in December 2001; the NHLR says the winter of 2002. The story gives both.
The 1994 contract, 1995 erection and 2019 Nugget give 65 ft; a 2016 blog gives 35 ft. The record uses 65 ft because it is supported by the contemporary coverage and the 2019 article.

notes_for_editor: Brief record errors: height_m 3.0 and design D-6 describe the cupola and the wrong structure; corrections proposed. The 1934 tower dimensions, collapse date and cupola date conflict across sources. Current staffing is only confirmed to 2019 (Nugget) and July 2016 (Cheryl Hill). No current access source was read beyond the 2016 blog, so the public-access level is provisional. Oregon.com, Oregon Hiking and Hikespeak showed up in search results and were not read; one gives 62 ft for the replacement, which is not used. The NHLR photos (1972 DNF archive; 2006 Ron Kemnow) have no URLs or licences, so none were added.
